questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign tells you a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle like a motorcycle really is. Do not guess at a small vehicle's speed or location.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then go normally.
Flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to where other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least ________ behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Use more distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Stay seated so the seat absorbs some impact.
Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: Which lane position is best to ride in?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcyclist to ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your way to escape.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your way to escape.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could hit you or block your escape route if something goes wrong.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A helmet will give you the most protection if it has all of these qualities, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: It is loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When you need to react to a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
Let other drivers know you are there by using your horn and lights or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for the situation and change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do these actions one at a time. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Position themselves where other drivers can see them.
Get ready to use the clutch and brakes quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, position yourself where other drivers can see you and be ready to use the clutch and brakes quickly. Slow down at intersections. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Eye protection is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection when riding. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while you are stopping on a straight road, you can leave it locked. You can usually keep control of your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if the motorcycle is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to avoid throwing off your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with lights flashing, change lanes to give it extra space and drive carefully. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: During the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards.
It stops you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to move your motorcycle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. This space also lets you safely move your motorcycle if needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should be used at all times.
Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually good, but groups should switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning or in a curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning or in a curve.
questions.explanation: Before your passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and your bike lean the right way.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you get hit by wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you get hit by wind blasts.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should protect you from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.
